title: The street that grows its own food
summary_es: Una calle que convirtió sus jardines en huertos. Preposiciones, cuantificadores, comparativos y relativos.
text: Ten years ago, the residents of a quiet street in the north of England decided to turn the small patches of grass in front of their houses {{1}} vegetable gardens. Nobody expected the idea to last. {{2}} of the neighbours had ever grown anything before, and the soil was poor. Today, however, the street produces {{3}} much fruit and veg that people regularly leave boxes of it outside their doors for anyone to take. The project has changed more {{4}} just the look of the street. Neighbours {{5}} used to nod politely to each other now spend their weekends working side by side. Children have learned where their food comes {{6}}, and several older residents say they feel far {{7}} lonely than before. Other streets have started copying the idea, and the local council is considering a plan to plant fruit trees in every park, {{8}} would make the whole town greener.

gaps.explanation_es: «Turn something into something» = convertir algo en otra cosa.
«Ever» pide una idea negativa: «none of the neighbours had ever…» (ninguno). «Few» (pocos) también vale.
«So much… that…» = tanto… que… Con nombres incontables se usa so much; con contables, so many.
Comparativo: «more than just…» = algo más que solo…
Relativo de persona como sujeto: who (o that). Aquí no se puede omitir.
«Come from». En las preguntas indirectas y con relativos, la preposición se queda al final: where their food comes from.
«Far less lonely than before» = mucho menos solos que antes. El «than» de después pide un comparativo.
«Which» tras coma se refiere a toda la idea anterior (lo cual). Después de una coma no se puede usar «that».
